newsletters.title: What Playing With AI Taught Me About My Work
newsletters.content:
AI can turn work into play—and distract me from the work I need to do. Here’s how I’m learning to bring something back from those detours.  ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌

WHAT PLAYING WITH AI TAUGHT ME ABOUT MY WORK https://every.?ev_audience=free


AI CAN TURN WORK INTO PLAY—AND DISTRACT ME FROM THE WORK I NEED TO DO. HERE’S HOW I’M LEARNING TO BRING SOMETHING BACK FROM THOSE DETOURS. https://every.?ev_audience=free

by Katie Parrott https://every.?ev_audience=free

Midjourney/Every illustration.

Was this newsletter forwarded to you? Sign up https://every.?ev_audience=free to get it in your inbox.



----------------------------------------



My childhood make-believe involved quite a bit of multitasking. I’d rollerblade in my front driveway for hours, bouncing a tennis ball on a racket and muttering dialogue for an elaborate storyline in which I was a Jane Austen heroine, or a 10th female member of the Fellowship of the Ring. Yes, I was incredibly cool.

That habit faded in my late teens, sort of like my religious faith https://every.?ev_audience=free did. Even at a tiny liberal arts college where people routinely wore cosplay around campus, I managed to lose touch with my imaginary people. Then adulthood happened, and I spent most of my twenties and early thirties learning to be employed and coexist peacefully with my brain.

Now, in my mid-30s, make-believe has made a big comeback and, yes, it’s thanks to AI. These days, my imaginary people come with websites and job descriptions.

Over Labor Day weekend, I spent a couple hundred dollars in tokens getting Astra https://every.?ev_audience=free to turn the skills in Compound Writing https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiIFdoY

howdy, it’s Barsee again.

happy thursday, AI family, and welcome back to AI Valley.

**here are the biggest things worth knowing today:**

* AI leaders are actually asking to slow AI down

* OpenAI isn’t going public this year

* Plus trending AI tools, posts, and resources

Let’s _dive_ into the Valley of AI…


----------

----------
#### **ADOBE**

## [New: Adobe Acrobat helps you unlock your own documents with new AI launch](https://business.adobe.com/products/acrobat-business.html)

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/9dea24fe-241a-4393-8690-b6413e57782f/FY26_Q3_PR_Stylize_Business_Report_1280x720.png?t=1788943761)

Caption: Courtesy: Adobe

Acrobat's new AI helps you understand documents faster, turning dense reports into visual summaries, interactive reports, podcasts, and audio experiences you can take anywhere. When it's time to share your work, Stylize transforms plain documents into polished deliverables in just a few clicks. Every answer includes clickable citations, and Adobe does not train on your document data.

_[See it for yourself with Acrobat Studio today.](https://business.adobe.com/products/acrobat-business.html)_

~_*This is sponsored_~


----------

----------
#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/d3f79d04-13a9-457f-8003-d6c8a501c726/image_-_2026-09-14T181721.899__1_.png?t=1789395453)
Caption: Courtesy: Ox45

**1/ AI leaders are actually asking to slow AI down** - Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei wrote a [3,800-word essay](https://darioamodei.com/post/we-must-pace-the-frontier) arguing that AI capabilities are moving too fast for safety work to keep up. Sam Altman, Elon Musk and DeepMind’s Demis Hassabis [basically agree](https://x.com/AISafetyMemes/status/2098944808844988480?s=20).

Amodei wants frontier labs to slow down, let outsiders test their models and eventually get countries to agree on some shared safety rules. His big worry is recursive self-improvement: AI getting good enough at AI research that it starts making better AI itself. He thinks we could be 6-12 months away from swarms of agents doing basically everything humans do on the internet.

The problem is nobody wants to be the first one to slow down. Trump [rejected](https://www.ft.com/content/cae60732-f929-4735-a627-db8c14e7c7ed?syn-25a6b1a6=1) calls for an AI slowdown. His argument is pretty simple: “whoever wins AI wins.”

And China said no too. The state-run Global Times [accused](https://x.com/kimmonismus/status/2099457575234179254?s=20) the US of trying to limit China’s AI progress through “technological barriers and regulatory monopolies,” calling the proposal a “silent AI Cold War.”

Funny enough, [AI 2027](https://ai-2027.com/) basically predicted this exact situation. In its scenario, experts start freaking out after the leading US lab develops a superhuman AI coder/researcher, but the president refuses to slow down because China might take the lead. We’re obviously not at the superhuman AI researcher bit yet... but the political argument is already here.

There are a couple other explanations for why the labs suddenly want to slow down. Maybe they’re worried about open-weight models catching up. Or maybe they’re all hitting the same walls and seeing something similar internally.

I’m not convinced they’re secretly staring at ASI though. If they were genuinely sitting on intelligence that could run circles around humanity, you’d expect to see some pretty ridiculous breakthroughs outside of chatbots too.

**2/ OpenAI isn’t going public this year** - despite confidentially filing for an IPO, Sam Altman says 2026 would be an “[ill-advised](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/12/openais-sam-altman-says-it-would-be-ill-advised-to-go-public-in-2026)” time to actually do it. OpenAI had reportedly been aiming for Q3/Q4 this year, but Altman now says “we’ve got a lot of stuff to do.”

Part of it is AI safety. Altman says OpenAI doesn’t want the pressure of being public while everything around the technology is moving this quickly, and that it’ll IPO when the business and “society” are ready.

There’s also the less philosophical bit: tech stocks have been volatile and OpenAI has its own financial challenges. The company is reportedly leaning toward 2027 instead.

So the OpenAI IPO is still coming... just probably not this year. ([watch Altman’s full interview here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2my-NU6LuCM))


----------

----------

Usage limits give my best questions—and my more questionable ideas—time to develop  ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌
https://every.?ev_audience=free


WHAT I LEARN WHEN I RUN OUT OF AI https://every.?ev_audience=free


USAGE LIMITS GIVE MY BEST QUESTIONS—AND MY MORE QUESTIONABLE IDEAS—TIME TO DEVELOP https://every.?ev_audience=free

by Jack Cheng https://every.?ev_audience=free

Midjourney/Every illustration.

Was this newsletter forwarded to you? Sign up https://every.?ev_audience=free to get it in your inbox.



----------------------------------------



I keep running out of access to the most capable AI models before the workweek is finished. Lately, I’ve come to realize that may be useful. Anthropic’s limits on both my work and personal Claude subscriptions reset at the start of the week. When they do, I gorge on the newly available capacity, running Fable on its highest effort levels and watching agents orchestrate subagents and dynamic workflows https://every.?ev_audience=free on multiple projects.

It used to be that I exhausted my weekly allocation within a day or so. I would go back to daily tasks with speedier, still-capable models like Sonnet https://every.?ev_audience=free and Sol https://every.?ev_audience=free, saving my biggest questions and one-shot builds and thorniest bugs until my limits reset.

The wait gives those questions time to develop. I’ve come to call my weekly sessions with the most powerful models “consulting the oracle”—a nod to the oracle at Delphi, where the ancient Greeks sought guidance from Apollo through the priestess Pythia (OK, also to The Matrix https://every.

howdy, it’s Barsee again.

happy friday, AI family, and welcome back to AI Valley.

**here are the biggest things worth knowing today:**

* OpenAI launches ChatGPT for financial services

* OpenAI also launched GPT-Live-1 in the API

* Anthropic threat team published a report on misusing Claude

* Plus trending AI tools, posts, and resources

Let’s _dive_ into the Valley of AI…


----------

----------
#### **WISPR FLOW**

## [Everywhere workflow (one voice layer across tools)](https://ref.wisprflow.ai/aivalley)

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/6945f9ec-3bdb-4e07-91f7-3d14b9c90031/Paid_Media_Newsletter_Image__6___1_.png?t=1789132860)

Caption: Courtesy: Wispr Flow

Flow is a voice layer that works anywhere you type. Use it to respond in Slack, write docs, craft emails, or prompt an AI assistant without switching tools or copy/pasting. It's the fastest way to get high-quality text into your workflow, whether you're drafting, editing, or ideating.

[Try Flow here](https://ref.wisprflow.ai/aivalley)

~_*This is sponsored_~


----------

----------
#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/830c0ff3-1dcc-457b-b8de-889b6fd8e0a5/finserv-source-picker-2x__1_.png?t=1789135523)
Caption: Courtesy: OpenAI

**1/ OpenAI made a ChatGPT specifically for finance** - [ChatGPT for Financial Services](https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-financial-services/) is a version of ChatGPT Work built around GPT-6 Astra, with financial data from Daloopa, PitchBook, LSEG News and Crunchbase already baked in. It’s built for research, financial models, pitchbooks and client materials.

Morgan Stanley and Evercore helped shape it, and OpenAI has integrations with S&P Capital IQ, MSCI, Moody’s and others so firms can also bring in data they already pay for.

The useful thing is Astra can dig through financial statements, tables and notes, do the analysis, then turn it into an Excel model, research note, deck or chart with the sources still there to check.

**_More OpenAI stuff:_**

* OpenAI also launched [GPT-Live-1 in the API](https://x.com/OpenAIDevs/status/2098099269551149398?s=20). It can listen and talk at the same time while models like Astra or Codex do the actual work behind it. Speak says it saw almost [80% fewer interruptions](https://x.com/speak/status/2098127080219345372?s=20), and it costs $0.05/minute before the backend model costs. So it roughly costs $72/day to run it 24/7 (much cheaper than i thought).

* And apparently OpenAI is thinking about [slowing down](https://www.wired.com/story/openai-wants-to-know-if-an-ai-industry-slowdown-would-even-be-legal/) frontier model development. Sam Altman reportedly brought up pacing development in an all-hands this week, and OpenAI has even asked Congress whether coordinating an AI slowdown could run into antitrust laws. The hope, obviously, is that everyone else slows down too.

**2/ Anthropic says it blocked possible efforts to build biological weapons** - Anthropic published its latest [Threat Report](https://www.anthropic.com/threat-intelligence-report-september-2026) covering misuse it shut down over the last eight months, including possible bioweapon research, espionage, surveillance and weapons development.

One case involved a scientist asking Claude for help with gain-of-function research on the chikungunya virus, including mutations that could make it more harmful. Anthropic says the work was apparently going to happen at a military research institute, which was enough for them to shut it down.

It also named seven Chinese AI labs, including Alibaba, DeepSeek, Moonshot and Xiaomi, that tried to distill Claude using thousands of fake accounts. Moonshot and DeepSeek were quietly relaying customer prompts to Claude through fraudulent accounts. Users thought they were using Chinese AI, but were actually getting answers from Claude.

Other cases include someone in Yemen using Claude Code to build rocket guidance software, a system designed to monitor 25M phone lines in Mali, 4,700 dating-app personas and malware rewritten to dodge antivirus software.

And this is with today’s models.

([you can read the report here](https://www.anthropic.com/threat-intelligence-report-september-2026))


----------

----------
# TRENDING TOOLS


--------------------
* [ChatGPT for Financial Services](https://x.com/OpenAI/status/2098118191029624911?s=20) - ChatGPT Work experience that combines built-in financial data with GPT-6 Astra’s reasoning

* [Devin Voice](https://x.com/cognition/status/2098142686486356185?s=20) - AI software engineer with a landline. You say it, Devin ships it. Powered by GPT-Live and our new SWE-2 model.

* [GPT-Live-1 API](https://x.com/OpenAIDevs/status/2098099269551149398?s=20) - bring ChatGPT’s natural back-and-forth to your app, with voice agents that listen while they speak and work with the models and harness you choose

* [Phoenix-4.5](https://x.com/tavus/status/2098085616663863427?s=20) - the fastest and most expressive real-time AI human rendering model on the market

* [Speak](https://www.speak.com/) - interactive language lessons with a tutor that get you talking, listens in real time, and helps you find your words

* [Data agent in ChatGPT Work](https://x.com/ChatGPT/status/2098065296968011853?s=20) - you can turn your company’s data into answers, interactive dashboards, and action just by asking

* [Gemini for Windows](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/products/gemini-app/gemini-app-now-on-windows/) - a native desktop app that opens over whatever you are doing with Alt+Space, reads context from Gmail and Drive, and carries the Gemini Spark agent

* [Google Labs’ Dreambeans](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/google-labs/dreambeans-expansion-september-2026) - it turns selected Gmail, Calendar, Photos, Search, YouTube, and Gemini context into finite daily reminders and recommendations

--------------------
